construct: Primary afferents carrying vibration, fine touch and proprioception ascend ipsilaterally in fasciculi gracilis/cuneatus and synapse in the gracile/cuneate nuclei of the caudal medulla. Second-order axons cross the midline as internal arcuate fibers and then ascend contralaterally as the medial lemniscus.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Vibration/proprioception fibers synapse in the gracile nucleus; their second-order axons cross in the caudal medulla as internal arcuate fibers before ascending as the medial lemniscus.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: The anterior white commissure is a plausible decussation site for sensory pathways but belongs to spinothalamic pain/temperature fibers, not dorsal-column modalities.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The nucleus-gracilis-to-medial-lemniscus sequence uniquely localizes the crossing to caudal-medullary internal arcuate fibers.
